discrepancies.title: Contaminated EXP-0037 Comparator

corrected_authoritative_exp0037_blind.label: EXP-0037 A4 Blind Benchmark Champion (EXP-0033 N=500)

discrepancies.root_cause: The previous EXP-0039 report mistakenly copied 90.75% from EXP-0038 development results on EXP-0025 (Docling HybridChunker C1 development accuracy) and combined it with the 18.50% FAR safety ceiling from EXP-0036. This conflated the development population (N=400) with the blind population (N=500).
discrepancies.recomputation_method: Extracted authentic metrics directly from committed lineage artifact EXP-0037-BLIND-RESULTS.json.
discrepancies.scientific_impact: Completely resolves historical reporting confusion. Development interventions are properly benchmarked against Control C0 (92.00% accuracy) on the same N=400 development population.

discrepancies.title: Defective Retrieval Metric Implementation (nDCG@5 > 100%)
discrepancies.root_cause: In scratch/run_exp0039_retrieval_benchmark.py lines 256-257, IDCG was hardcoded as idcg = 1.0 / np.log2(2), assuming binary relevance with only 1 relevant chunk. In semantic chunking, fine-grained proposition chunking causes an average of 4.8 to 5.1 chunks per query to match the curriculum rule. When multiple matching chunks appeared in top-5, DCG summed up to 2.56, producing nDCG values > 100% when divided by 1.0.
discrepancies.recomputation_method: Applied standard bounded nDCG@5 formula where IDCG@5 is the ideal discounted cumulative gain for min(|Gold|, 5) relevant chunks: IDCG@5 = sum_{r=1}^{min(|G|, 5)} 1 / log2(r + 1). Strictly bounded in [0%, 100%].
discrepancies.scientific_impact: Retrieval Recall@5 remains 100.0% for all conditions. Corrected nDCG@5 reveals that semantic chunking achieves 86.02% (due to multiple granular chunks sharing relevance) while providing superior downstream verifier precision.

discrepancies.title: Paired Contingency Table Subscript Inversion (n01 vs n10)

corrected_recomputed_values.convention: n01 = baseline incorrect, candidate correct; n10 = baseline correct, candidate incorrect

discrepancies.root_cause: The previous code inverted the subscript notation, assigning n01 to 'C0 only' and n10 to 'Candidate only'. Under standard paired contingency convention, n01 represents the candidate winning (baseline=0, candidate=1) and n10 represents the baseline winning (baseline=1, candidate=0).
discrepancies.recomputation_method: Direct vectorized computation from scratch/exp0039_dev_predictions.json without altering any prediction.
discrepancies.scientific_impact: Restores mathematical consistency between table counts, forensic narrative, and delta: delta = 100 * (n01 - n10) / 400.

discrepancies.title: OOD Recall Reporting Text Inconsistency for C2_085
discrepancies.root_cause: Typographical error in narrative text. Case DEV-UNK-010 (SQLAlchemy/Alembic) was predicted SUPPORTED by C2_085, yielding 99/100 correct (99.00%). The JSON result already had 99.00%, but the text claimed 100.00%.
discrepancies.recomputation_method: Count of correct predictions in OUT_OF_CURRICULUM_UNKNOWN category (99 / 100).
discrepancies.scientific_impact: Ensures complete alignment between narrative claims and exact confusion matrix.

discrepancies.title: C1 FRR Arithmetic Inconsistency
discrepancies.root_cause: Original script computed C1 FRR as 25/150 (only counting Supported->Refuted), omitting 2 Supported->Not_Established false abstentions. Total rejected supported claims = 27 / 150 = 18.00%, which aligns with FRR = 100% - Supported Recall (82.00%).
discrepancies.scientific_impact: Restores arithmetic consistency across all confusion matrix derivations.
